news.title: Housing may shape death risks for low-income older renters
news.summary_en: For low-income older adults, where they live may affect how long they live, according to new research from Washington University in St. Louis.

news.title: Five trends shaping public health
news.summary_en: From longer lives to eroding institutional trust, powerful forces are converging in ways that demand new approaches to protecting human health.

news.title: CAPS students help Trailnet create safer streets
news.summary_en: WashU Continuing & Professional Studies students mapped collision patterns and the city’s busiest corridors — work that supports Trailnet’s mission to make St. Louis streets safer and more accessible for pedestrians, cyclists, transit riders and drivers.

news.title: Technique evaluates reliability of imaging measurements used in medical decision-making
news.summary_en: Advances in medical imaging and artificial intelligence have revolutionized many aspects of medical practice, but it can be hard to know if a given measurement tool works as intended. A technique developed by WashU researchers can be used to assess the reliability of quantitative imaging tools.

news.title: Newly found ‘immune organ’ inside skull directs brain defense
news.summary_en: WashU Medicine researchers discovered immune hubs in the skull bone marrow responsible for mounting a rapid immune response in the brain, which may point to new ways to fight brain cancer and neurodegenerative diseases.
